snippet.title: Arsenio Hall on Magic Johnson Revealing HIV Status
snippet.description:
http://www.vladtv.com - For those who didn't know, in 1991 Earvin "Magic" Johnson revealed his positive HIV status to the world on the Arsenio Hall Show, and during a recent interview with VladTV, Arsenio reflected on the emotional struggles he dealt with while being present for the announcement with Magic.

Arsenio explained that because of his close friendship with Magic, he wasn't thrilled with the idea of the basketball star making the announcement on his platform, and urged him to instead reveal his HIV status on a different talk show.  However, Magic insisted on addressing the public on Arsenio's show because he felt "comfortable" there.  

During a phone conversation between Magic and Arsenio the morning before the show was set to shoot, Magic made a very important request to his friend. "You got something else you got to do dog.  You got to help me live forever, man."

Be sure to tune into the Arsenio Hall Show on the WPIX channel in New York, KTLA in Los Angeles, WGN in Chicago, and other varying channels across the United States, late night, Monday through Friday.

snippet.title: The Day Magic Johnson Shocked the World: His 1991 HIV Announcement
snippet.description:
On November 7, 1991, the basketball world changed forever.

Los Angeles Lakers superstar Magic Johnson held a press conference and announced that he had tested positive for HIV. At just 32 years old, one of the biggest stars in professional sports suddenly announced his retirement from the NBA.

The news shocked fans, teammates, opponents, and people around the world.

But Magic Johnson's story didn't end with that announcement.

He became an important public advocate for HIV awareness and helped challenge misconceptions and stigma surrounding the virus. In 1992, Magic returned to the NBA All-Star Game, and he later returned to the Lakers during the 1995–96 season.

More than three decades later, his 1991 announcement remains one of the most significant moments in sports history—not simply because it changed the career of an NBA superstar, but because it brought enormous public attention to HIV awareness.

This is the story of the day Magic Johnson stepped away from basketball and began a completely different chapter of his life.

snippet.title: The Day Magic Johnson Shocked the Entire World
snippet.description: On November 7, 1991, Magic Johnson held a press conference and announced he had tested HIV positive and was retiring from the NBA. The sports world — and the entire country — was stunned. At a time when HIV was still heavily stigmatized, Magic’s announcement forced millions of adults to confront the disease head-on and changed public perception forever. snippet.title: Magic Johnson was given less than a year to live in 1991. He is still alive 34 years later.
snippet.description:
On November 7, 1991, Magic Johnson called a press conference to announce he had tested positive for HIV and was immediately retiring from the NBA. He was 32 years old. At the time, HIV was widely considered a death sentence. Most medical experts gave him less than one year to live.

Earvin "Magic" Johnson was the greatest point guard in basketball history. At 6'9", he was the tallest point guard ever to play in the NBA. He won 3 NBA Most Valuable Player awards, 5 NBA championships with the Los Angeles Lakers, and was Finals MVP at age 20.

What happened after his diagnosis defied every prediction. Months after retiring, he played in the 1992 NBA All-Star Game and won MVP. He was selected to the Dream Team that won gold at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics. He came back to play 32 more games for the Lakers in 1996.

He did not die.

Magic Johnson has been HIV positive for 34 years. He is 65 years old today. After his playing career, he built one of the most successful business empires in American sports. He owns parts of the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Washington Commanders. He is worth more than $1 billion.

In 1991, doctors gave Magic Johnson one year to live. He outlived the prediction by 34 years and built a billion-dollar empire while doing it.
